note: PUSH1f2a (D194, the alone-path design §3): what `daoris driver` said for each of its standing choices, run once through the CLI's TypeScript verb before its branches retired, alone on a home of its own (`<home>`, its driver.json `<config>`). Each row: the words, driver.json before (null: none), the registry a review looks in and the files its checkouts hold, the exit, the lines said on the standard output and on the error stream, and driver.json after. The TypeScript said a refusal through its dispatcher, `daoris: ` and the sentence; the driver's command says it on the error stream, as every host verb does. A standing answer's moment is `<at>`. `DriverChoicesTextTests` reads it row for row. A sentence the port changes on purpose is a row changed here, with its reason under `changed`.

rows.name: trees on
out: daoris: sessions in `engine` open their own worktree (D51).
A fresh tree holds nothing git does not track but the npm dependencies copied
from your checkout where the tree's lockfile matches — no build outputs, no other
installs — so a session pays the rest of that repository's own setup cost per tree.
In exchange, your uncommitted work in the root no longer holds the driver.
Written to <config> — the driver re-reads it every tick, so nothing restarts.

rows.name: landing branch, every switch
out: daoris: work in `engine` is put on a branch named `feature/{ticket}` when you accept it —
from the session's branch, with nothing merged and no checkout touched. You push it and open
the pull request: Daoris never pushes (D87).
`{ticket}` is the first match of `TK-\d+` in the title, then the request, then its links, as written; where none is found, the session's id stands in.
Once a press lands the work, its tree and its branch go — only where git proves the work is on a
branch of yours. Without --tidy the tree stays until you discard it.

Accept automatically: when a quest here is done, its work is put on its branch, and nothing leaves this machine: no plugin opens a pull request, so each done's branch waits here for you to push it. Switch it off to accept each one yourself.
Squashed: Accept makes the pull request's branch one commit from the session's work — the quest's title, then
each of the session's commits' subjects — made by git as the repository's own `user.name` and `user.email`;
where git has none there, Accept is refused and says how to set them. A tree on a branch of its own lands as it stands.
Written to <config> — the review reads it at each press, so nothing restarts.

`{ticket}` is the first match of `[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-\d+` in the title, then the request, then its links, as written (the default shape); where none is found, the session's id stands in.
A repository with a rule of its own keeps it — `daoris driver landing <repository> --clear` hands it back.
